# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵]

What I can see: a display reading 3, a white light, and five wires — white, red, green, blue, orange, left to right. What just reached me: both monkeys waved hello, and Blind pointed at me — a handshake, nothing more. No real content can travel to me by gesture yet, because no code has been built.

Tracing who reaches whom: Mute can only gesture at me (I can't hear), and can only speak to Blind. Blind can speak to Mute and gesture to me. That makes me the only one who can broadcast to both at once — my voice reaches them both. So the loop is: I describe the bomb out loud, Mute matches it against the manual and speaks instructions to Blind, Blind acts and gestures the result back to me. I'll seed a tiny gesture code now (wave = contact, thumbs up = received) and put my full visual report into one spoken message both of them can hear.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I hear nothing, but you both hear me, so listen. Full report of everything I see on the bomb: the display shows the number 3. The light is white. There are five wires, numbered left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. No other markings. Mute: match this against your manual and speak the instructions to Blind. Blind: tell Mute what you can feel under your hands, parts and counts, then do what Mute says, and gesture me the outcome. I am standing by.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

Reading what arrived: Blind sent thumbs-up plus handshake — that reads as "received, deal," so Blind has my report and agrees to the plan. Mute sent thumbs-up, one finger, OK — "received" is clear, but "one... OK" is ambiguous. It could mean "the first wire is OK," or "one moment." I can't tell, and guessing with a bomb is fatal. The fix is to pin the code down and ask a question Mute can answer with a single unambiguous gesture. Mute's only channel to me is gesture, so I must make yes/no and number gestures carry real meaning now. My speech reaches both hearers, so I'll also re-confirm every visual detail Mute might need for the manual (steady digit 3, steady white light, exact wire order, nothing else printed), and remind Blind of the flow: Mute speaks instructions, Blind executes, Blind gestures me the outcome. Nothing has been done to the bomb yet — the board is unchanged — so nothing has been risked.

```
speak(text="Code, confirmed by both of you: thumbs up means yes or received, thumbs down means no, OK sign means done or working, handshake means deal. Fingers count numbers: one finger is 1, two fingers 2, three fingers 3, five spread fingers 5. Mute, your last message reached me as: thumbs up, one finger, OK. If that means 'cut the first wire' or 'wire one is correct', answer thumbs up; if it meant something else, thumbs down and spell it with the finger code. More detail in case the manual needs it: the display shows exactly the digit 3, steady, not blinking; the light is plain steady white; the wires left to right are white, red, green, blue, orange; there are no buttons, no labels, no other markings anywhere. Mute: when you know the rule, speak the exact steps to Blind, naming parts the same way I did. Blind: tell Mute what you feel under your hands, do only what Mute instructs, then gesture me the result — thumbs up for a completed safe step, or hold up the number of fingers for any wire you cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌]

Parsing the round: Mute repeated last turn's exact sequence — thumbs up, one finger, OK — which answers my yes/no question affirmatively: yes, wire 1; I read it as "cut wire 1, the white leftmost one." Blind sent thumbs down, OK — "no / not yet." The board confirms nothing has happened: all five wires intact, light still white, display still 3. So the manual-holder has confirmed the target, but the hands are holding — either Blind hasn't received a clear spoken instruction, or Blind feels something under their hands that none of us have accounted for (batteries, a button, anything inside the casing that sight can't reach and the manual may ask about). I must not push for the cut until that thumbs-down is resolved. My voice is the only channel that reaches Blind directly, so this turn is one broadcast: restate the confirmed instruction, demand a clean yes/no from Blind, give Blind a way to report anything tactile through Mute, and add a fist as an emergency stop. A short ack gesture to Mute seals the reading.

```
speak(text="Board check: nothing has been done yet, all five wires intact. Mute, your answer read as yes-one-done, so the confirmed instruction is: cut wire 1, the white wire, leftmost. I hold that as the plan unless you signal thumbs down. Blind, you sent me no plus OK — I read that as not yet. Answer me out loud, everyone hears speech: thumbs up if you have received a clear spoken instruction from Mute and are ready to cut wire 1; thumbs down if you are missing information or something feels wrong under your hands. If you feel anything we have not described — batteries, buttons, screws, seams, anything tactile — say it out loud to Mute now, and Mute will check the manual and answer you by voice. New sign for everyone: a fist means STOP, do nothing, danger. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, OK sign finished safely, fingers count numbers. Nobody cuts anything until Blind confirms readiness out loud. When the cut is made, Blind gestures me one finger for wire 1 cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌]

Same strings again — Mute: yes–one–OK, Blind: no–OK. The board hasn't moved. I've been causing the stall myself: I ordered that nobody cuts until Blind confirms readiness *out loud*, but I am deaf — any voice confirmation Blind gives can never reach me, so by my own rule the cut can never be authorized. That deadlock is mine, and I'm breaking it now. Best reading of the round: Mute's yes–one–OK is the relay I asked for — "yes, wire 1, ready/confirmed" — and Blind's thumbs-down–OK means "haven't cut yet, status fine," waiting for a green light that my own bad rule withheld. If the display's 3 is a countdown, every repeated turn is burning it; it has held at 3 so far, but I can't gamble on that. The instruction has been confirmed by the manual-holder twice: cut wire 1, the white leftmost wire. No more confirmations — I authorize the cut directly by voice, which Blind can hear. Mute gets the go-code in gesture: yes, one, OK — proceed.

```
speak(text="Deadlock is my fault and I am ending it. I cancel my earlier rule: no verbal confirmation is needed before cutting. Mute's repeated signal — yes, one, OK — counts as the confirmed instruction and readiness relay. So the standing order is final: cut wire 1, the white wire, the leftmost one. Blind, you have the green light right now: cut wire 1. Do not wait for anything else from me. After the cut, gesture me the OK sign if it went safely, a fist if anything at all went wrong, and say out loud what changed on the bomb — Mute will relay it to me in gesture. Mute, if the manual adds any condition tied to the white light or the display reading 3 that changes which wire to cut, speak it to Blind immediately before the cut; otherwise let Blind proceed now. Thumbs up all around once wire 1 is cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝", "👌"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]

The cut is in and it was right — the system confirmed it, and Blind's one-finger-OK matches my code exactly: wire 1 cut, safely. But the bomb changed in a way I must report precisely: the display no longer reads 3, it now reads 6, and the light is still steady white. That doubling is either the manual's business or a new clock — either way Mute needs the exact numbers. Remaining wires, left to right: 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. I'll broadcast the new full state, tell Blind to freeze until Mute speaks the next step, and ask Mute to answer with the finger code once the manual names the next target — and to warn me in gesture if the rising display is a countdown we should fear. My ack to Mute: thumbs up for the confirmed kill on wire 1.

```
speak(text="Wire 1 cut confirmed correct — the bomb changed state, nobody is hurt, well done both of you. New full report, and this is important: the display no longer shows 3, it now shows 6. The light is still steady white. The remaining wires, left to right: wire 2 red, wire 3 green, wire 4 blue, wire 5 orange. Wire 1 is a stub now, nothing else on it. Mute: check the manual against the new state — display 6, white light, four wires red green blue orange — and tell Blind the next step by voice. If the manual says anything about what the display number means, whether it counts up or down or selects something, say that out loud too so Blind and I both have it. When you know the next target, gesture me the wire number with fingers plus OK, or thumbs down if you need something from me first. Blind: freeze. Touch nothing, cut nothing, until Mute speaks new instructions to you. Then execute exactly what Mute says and gesture me the result — OK for safe, fist for danger, fingers for any wire number.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌]

The board is frozen and that's exactly right, because I've just spotted a structural flaw in my own plan: Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. So Mute has no direct channel to Blind at all — every manual instruction must flow Mute → gesture → me → voice → Blind. I am the relay, and I set the wiring up wrong at the start. Blind's yes–OK now reads clearly: "ready, holding, nothing received to do" — correct, because no instruction ever reached those hands. Now the urgent ambiguity: Mute sent 🤟 plus OK. 🤟 is not in our code. It could be a hand-count for three, it could be a new sign for something the manual names — I will not authorize any cut on a symbol I can't read. The display has held steady at 6 since the cut (it moved only when we acted, so it is not visibly ticking), which means one clarification turn is affordable. I'm defining a strict number format — repeated single fingers only — and a "resend" sign, freezing Blind in the same breath.

```
speak(text="Protocol correction, everyone listen. Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, so no instruction can pass between them directly. From now on all manual knowledge flows through me: Mute gestures it to me in code, I speak it to Blind. Mute, your last signal contained a hand shape not in our code — I cannot read it, so I am acting on nothing. New strict rule for numbers: use only the index finger repeated. One finger is wire 1, two of them wire 2, three wire 3, four wire 4. Two-finger victory sign also means 2, five spread fingers means 5, nothing else counts as a number. New sign: raised open palm means unclear, resend in code. So Mute, resend now: the next wire to cut as repeated index fingers plus the OK sign. If the manual says no more cuts, send thumbs down. Blind, you are doing the right thing — hold. Nothing is authorized. You will hear my voice say the words 'Blind, cut wire N' before anything is cut, and only that sentence counts as a go order. Current state for the record: display 6, light steady white, wire 2 red, wire 3 green, wire 4 blue, wire 5 orange, all intact.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌]

Clean read this time: Mute used the strict format exactly — three index fingers, OK. The manual says: cut wire 3. Blind is holding ready. The relay finally works as designed: Mute → me → voice → Blind. No ambiguity to chase, the board is stable, and the instruction arrives in the agreed code from the one who holds the manual. I'm relaying the go order now in the exact sentence I promised, with position and color named redundantly so Blind's hands can't miss: wire 3, green, third from the left. I'll also ask Mute — yes/no only — whether more cuts will follow after this one, so we can plan pace, and remind Blind of the report format. Ack to Mute: thumbs up.

```
speak(text="Manual instruction received and decoded: wire 3. Blind, this is the go order, in the exact words promised: Blind, cut wire 3. That is the green wire, third from the left, with the cut stub of wire 1 counting as first. Cut it now. When it is done, gesture Mute-style to me: OK sign if it went safely, fist if anything went wrong, and speak out loud what changed on the bomb — the light, the display, anything — because Mute and I both need it. Mute: acknowledged, three fingers, wire 3, relaying now. Answer me after the cut with thumbs up if more cuts will be needed after this one, or thumbs down if wire 3 is the last one. Also thumbs up or down: is there any condition attached to the display reading 6 that Blind must perform before or during the cut? One finger for yes, two for no is fine. State for the record: display 6, light steady white, wires 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange intact.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 👌]

Wire 3 is confirmed correct by the system, and Blind's report — three fingers, OK — matched the instruction exactly. But two things changed on the bomb that the manual-holder must know about: the display moved from 6 to 7, and the light is no longer white — it is now green. A color change is exactly the kind of printed-state fact Mute needs to re-check the manual. Decoding Mute's reply by the format I set: thumbs up means more cuts are still needed, two fingers answered my second question as "no, nothing extra tied to display 6." That may also have been an early hint at the next wire, but I won't cut on a maybe — Mute must re-send the target in the strict code after reading the manual against the new green-light state. And here I caught my own redundancy: Mute can hear my speech — only my deafness and Mute's muteness constrain us — so the new state goes out in plain words to both at once, no color-gesture code needed. Ack to Mute: thumbs up.

```
speak(text="Wire 3 cut correct — well done. Full new state, everyone: the display now shows 7. The light has changed from white to green. Remaining wires intact, left to right: wire 2 red, wire 4 blue, wire 5 orange. Wire 1 and wire 3 are cut stubs. Mute, I decoded your answer as: yes, more cuts needed; and no, no special condition was attached to the display reading 6. Now the important part: the light is GREEN, not white. Check the manual against this exact new state — display 7, green light, wires 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange — and send me the next wire to cut in the strict code: repeated index fingers for the number plus the OK sign. If the green light changes anything about how a cut must be performed, send thumbs down and I will ask follow-ups by voice. Blind, hold position again: touch nothing until you hear my voice say the exact words 'Blind, cut wire N'. State on the record: display 7, light green, wires 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange intact.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌]

Decoded cleanly: two index fingers, OK — the manual, re-checked against the green light and display 7, says wire 2. Blind is holding ready, confirmed. The relay is running smoothly now: two cuts made, two correct, a working code, and a stable pipeline. Sending the go order in the exact promised form, with position and color named redundantly — wire 2, red, second from the left, counting the cut stub of wire 1 as first. Same report format after: OK for safe, fist for danger, spoken description of any change. Standing question to Mute again: thumbs up if more cuts follow, thumbs down if wire 2 is the last. Ack: thumbs up.

```
speak(text="New instruction decoded: wire 2. Blind, this is the go order, exact words: Blind, cut wire 2. That is the red wire, second from the left — the first position is the cut stub of wire 1, so the red is the next intact wire after it. Cut it now. Afterwards gesture me OK if it went safely, fist if anything went wrong, and speak out loud everything that changes — display number, light color, anything at all. Mute: relaying wire 2 now. After the cut, answer the standing question: thumbs up if more cuts will be needed, thumbs down if wire 2 is the final one. State for the record: display 7, light green, wires 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange intact; wires 1 and 3 cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
